sentences.text: In a solar eclipse the Moon passes exactly between the Sun and Earth and its shadow falls on Earth.
This time the Moon is in the far half of its orbit, so it looks slightly smaller than the Sun in the sky: it cannot cover it fully and a bright ring of fire remains.
Let us look from the centre of the shadow: the Moon's dark disc settles onto the middle of the Sun.
The path of annularity runs from the South Pacific across Chile and Argentina to the Atlantic; a partial eclipse is seen across wide areas of South America and Africa.
The next great eclipse comes on 2 August 2027: a six-minute total eclipse crossing Egypt and Saudi Arabia.
